Market share can be computed without knowing total sales of all firms in the market.
Secondary data are primary when downloaded from a government website by an employee.
Primary data are secondary when the sample size exceeds one thousand respondents.
Market volume sums current sales of all competing firms offering the product in the market.
tactical_explanations:
Market size is total sales of all businesses.

Because that detail fails, the whole statement fails even if the topic word looks familiar.

The statement is false.

Total market sales are required in the denominator.

The absolute wording "all" turns a familiar idea into an overclaim. One ordinary counterexample is enough to reject it.

The statement is false.

Download method does not make prior research primary.

Because that detail fails, the whole statement fails even if the topic word looks familiar.

The statement is false.

Large samples still produce primary information.

Because that detail fails, the whole statement fails even if the topic word looks familiar.

The statement is false.

All rival sales sum to market volume.

That is exactly what the claim asserts, so the wording survives a careful check against the standard idea.

The statement is true.

title: Free Secondary Research Availability
context: Analyze an example where fifteen per cent absolute share against a leader's thirty per cent yields relative share of 0.5. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Sales potential exceeds sales volume when the firm could win additional buyers not yet captured.
Customer analysis excludes prospective buyers and studies only past purchasers.
Seasonal fluctuations cannot inform production planning according to customer-analysis timing data.
Motive research cannot affect market-share strategies because share is fixed by regulation.
Gains from competitors are part of market volume rather than sales potential.
tactical_explanations:
Uncaptured buyers raise sales potential above volume.

That is exactly what the claim asserts, so the wording survives a careful check against the standard idea.

The statement is true.

Prospective buyers are within research scope.

Because that detail fails, the whole statement fails even if the topic word looks familiar.

The statement is false.

Timing analysis supports planning ahead for seasonal demand.

The absolute wording "cannot" turns a familiar idea into an overclaim. One ordinary counterexample is enough to reject it.

The statement is false.

Motives inform development and share enhancement.

The absolute wording "cannot" turns a familiar idea into an overclaim. One ordinary counterexample is enough to reject it.

The statement is false.

Gains from competitors belong to sales potential.

Because that detail fails, the whole statement fails even if the topic word looks familiar.

The statement is false.
